text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday as reported by the official Algerian news agency APS. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Transitional National Council's deputies reject Arabic language draft law to extend the use of the language in government administration, universities and business.
- National security chief says civilian population has cornered the terrorists.
- World Bank experts debate privatisation with Algerian officials and specialists to seek ways to speed up the sell-off process.
- Arab states' police start 20th congress in Algiers to chart a common strategy to fight organised crime and terrorism.

- German junior foreign minister Werner Hoyer, accompanied by large delegation of businessmen, hold talks with Algerian officials over cooperation. The Germans are also interested in the Algerian energy sector.
